title: Remap genomic annotations between assemblies with liftOver

sources.locator: whole document; chain-file construction and Ensembl genePred example

scientific_use: Map genomic feature coordinates and supported annotation formats from an old assembly to a new assembly using a chain alignment, yielding mapped and unmapped records. The source describes producing chain maps from genome assemblies and using them to lift annotations; it warns that same-organism assembly changes are the intended case and cross-species mappings are not sufficient for homology inference.
tool_role_basis: The documented operation applies the existing liftOver command and chain map to annotation files. Its underlying implementation is inspected only to establish interface semantics.
inputs: Old-assembly BED by default, or supported genePred, GFF/GTF, sample, PSL-target, position, or BED-plus records; provide oldFile and a chain file with old genome on target and new genome on query.
Chain files are upstream alignments; the source document outlines BLAT, axtChain, chainNet, and chainNetSubset stages for generating them.
outputs: Mapped annotation records in requested output file and records that failed mapping in a separate unmapped file; output coordinates refer to query/new assembly.
dependencies: UCSC kent liftOver binary and chain-format map for the selected assembly pair.
For generating chain maps, source lists UCSC alignment and chain/net tools plus assembly FASTA/chromosome-size files; historical example uses cluster resources and is not validated here.
evidence: src/hg/liftOver/liftOver.c usage states input/output formats, chain direction, output files, supported flags, and same-organism caveat.
src/hg/doc/liftOver.txt explains chain construction and shows lifting an ensGene genePred table.
limitations: The documentation itself says the instructions are untested; do not treat as a verified runbook.
No specific assembly pair, chain asset, or annotation study dataset is pinned. Cross-species use needs independent biological justification.
Mapping quality thresholds and acceptable loss need task-specific decisions; genePred/GFF feature integrity requires downstream validation.

title: Summarize bigWig signal over BED regions
source_kind: command-line tool implementation and usage text

sources.locator: file header and usage(); addBigWigIntervalInfo(); averageFetchingEachChrom(); bigWigAverageOverBed()

scientific_use: For each BED interval, compute covered bases, signal sum, mean with uncovered bases treated as zero (mean0), mean over covered bases, and optionally min/max. BED12 block intervals are summarized across blocks, so exon-like intervals can exclude introns; optional center-window sampling offers a distinct measurement window.
tool_role_basis: The source provides a ready command applying bigWig signal queries to a BED region set and emitting summaries; the task would use the existing program.
inputs: A bigWig numeric signal track and BED intervals with unique names; BED12 blocks are respected. Inputs must share chromosome names and coordinate reference.
Optional sampleAroundCenter=N substitutes a fixed-width interval centered on each BED item.
outputs: Tabular per-item name, size, covered, sum, mean0, mean, and optional min/max; optional BED echo with appended statistic and optional overall stats RA file.
dependencies: UCSC kent bigWig and BED readers; a locally or remotely accessible bigWig and matching interval file.
evidence: Usage text defines input/output columns and options.

bigWigAverageOverBed() loads BED, enforces unique names, opens bigWig and selects block-wise or chromosome-wise calculation; chromosome path handles missing bigWig chromosomes by reporting zero coverage.
limitations: No concrete biological signal track or region set is identified in the inspected source, so dataset_ids is empty.
Output semantics distinguish mean over covered bases from mean0; graders must preserve this distinction.
Remote access behavior, runtime, and memory requirements were not tested.

title: Filter multiallelic VCF records by alternate allele count
source_kind: command-line tool implementation and regression fixture

sources.locator: usage(), getExcludeChromPos(), filterMinAcFromGenotypes(), filterMinAcFromInfo(), printWithNewAlts(), and vcfFilter()

scientific_use: Remove variant records by exact CHROM/POS exclusion and/or discard alternate alleles below a minimum allele count. With genotype columns, the tool tallies monoploid genotypes, updates AC and AN and recodes genotypes; without genotype columns it reads AC from INFO. It can rename variants from REF, POS, and surviving ALT alleles.
tool_role_basis: The source shows use of an existing VCF transformation program on VCF inputs; implementation inspection establishes its operation and limitations.
inputs: VCF with #CHROM header and at least eight columns; optional monoploid genotype columns, whose alleles are tallied when present.
Optional exclusion VCF; only CHROM and POS are used and chromosome names must match exactly.
The repository test input declares reference NC_045512v2 and source faToVcf from refPlus.unmapped.aligned.fasta; see dataset record for fixture provenance limits.
outputs: VCF on stdout, retaining headers and records with at least one surviving alternate allele; INFO AC is updated, AN and genotype allele indexes updated when genotypes are used, optional IDs are generated from REF/POS/ALT.
dependencies: UCSC kent vcfFilter binary and standard kent C libraries.
For exclusion filtering, a VCF whose chromosome naming and coordinate convention match the primary input.
evidence: usage() documents exclusion and minimum allele count behavior and monoploid genotype restriction.
filterMinAcFromGenotypes() tallies ALT indexes from monoploid genotype columns and recodes indexes; filterMinAcFromInfo() uses AC in INFO.
tests/makefile compares command output with expected VCFs for rename, filtering with/without genotype columns, and exclusion.
limitations: The implementation explicitly rejects diploid/polyploid separator syntax and was written for SARS-CoV-2 data; this is not a general diploid VCF filter.

Test VCF source metadata identifies reference NC_045512v2 and faToVcf origin, but the generating aligned FASTA, exact observations/source accessions, and licensing are not established by inspected materials.
The test fixture is a source-level example only; command execution was not performed.

title: Extract reference sequence intervals from twoBit into FASTA
source_kind: command-line tool implementation, usage text, and regression workflow

sources.locator: test target commands over whole sequences, fragments, sequence lists, and BED

scientific_use: Extract all sequences, named sequences, coordinate fragments, listed ranges, or BED-defined intervals from an indexed twoBit reference into FASTA. BED12 blocks concatenate exonic blocks without introns and negative-strand items are reverse-complemented; optional noMask uppercases masked sequence.
tool_role_basis: The program applies a pre-existing reference-sequence extraction tool to a supplied genome asset and coordinates.
inputs: twoBit reference genome file or documented UCSC hg38 URL, plus optional sequence name/range, sequence-list file, or BED intervals.
Coordinate fragments use zero-based half-open intervals; BED input can provide multiple regions and BED12 block layout.
outputs: FASTA records for selected sequence(s); with BED input, one sequence per interval, preserving BED name unless bedPos is requested.
dependencies: UCSC kent twoBitToFa executable and twoBit reader libraries.
Reference twoBit assembly asset and optional BED/list file using chromosome names for that assembly.
evidence: usage() defines twoBit input, range conventions, sequence-list and BED modes, and documents an hg38 twoBit URL example.
twoBitAndBedToSeq() joins blocks, excludes introns, and reverse-complements negative-strand records.
The makefile enumerates fixture usage for whole-file extraction, slices, sequence lists, and BED input.
limitations: The documented hg38 URL contains a mutable `latest` path; no immutable assembly release/checksum or terms were inspected.
Repository test twoBit fixtures are tiny test assets and do not identify a biological dataset; the external reference asset is a separate candidate support record.
No extraction was executed; masking, boundary behavior, and output suitability remain unvalidated for a task-specific asset.

title: Load user annotations into the Genome Browser as a custom track

sources.locator: guided walkthrough Steps 1-5, track line, and data format guidance

scientific_use: Prepare and display user-provided annotations in the UCSC Genome Browser at a chosen assembly and region. The tutorial covers browser/track metadata, accepted annotation formats, upload or URL loading, and opening the data in related browser tools.
tool_role_basis: The tutorial shows using the existing custom-track interface and supported formats to inspect user annotations; it does not create an annotation algorithm.
inputs: User annotation in a supported track format and compatible assembly/chromosome naming; optional browser position and track name/description/display settings.
Binary-indexed formats such as bigBed, bigWig, BAM, CRAM, or VCF require externally hosted files, according to the tutorial.
outputs: Temporary browser custom track with visualized annotations and links to Genome Browser, Table Browser, Data Integrator, or Variant Annotation Integrator.
dependencies: UCSC Genome Browser custom-track service and assembly selection.
External hosting for binary-indexed files; the tutorial says custom tracks are automatically discarded 48 hours after last access.
evidence: Tutorial documents assembly choice, browser position line, track line attributes, accepted format guidance, upload/URL loading, and linked tools.
It says chromosome naming may use UCSC-style names or aliases and lists indexed formats that must be hosted externally.
limitations: This is an interactive display workflow, not a quantitative validation or durable data-storage workflow.
No actual annotation, assembly pair, or hosted file is identified; genome build compatibility and data license remain caller responsibilities.
The 48-hour discard claim and service behavior derive from current-at-revision tutorial text and were not independently tested.

title: Convert genePred gene models to BED12 exon blocks

title: Select, filter, intersect, and export genome browser track data

sources.locator: guided walkthrough Steps 1-5 and Optional: filter, subset, or combine tracks

scientific_use: Query genome browser tracks by assembly, track/table, genomic region or identifier list; apply row filters, intersect/anti-intersect with another track, and export selected table fields, BED/GTF/custom-track formats, or sequence. The tutorial names variant overlap with RefSeq coding exons and region overlap with peak tracks as example questions.
tool_role_basis: The tutorial describes using the existing UCSC Table Browser interface to query existing tracks and export results, without implementing a new analysis tool.
inputs: Genome assembly, track and table; region coordinates, gene name, uploaded/pasted region or identifier list, or genome-wide selection.
Optional filter conditions and a second track for overlap or non-overlap comparisons; examples include SNPs against RefSeq coding exons and regions against peak tracks.
outputs: Selected rows or related-table fields; optional BED, GTF, custom track, DNA sequence, or protein sequence output, depending on selected track and format.
dependencies: UCSC Genome Browser Table Browser service and selected assembly's hosted track/table data.
Track schema and related-table metadata to select fields or join related tables.
evidence: The tutorial's overview identifies the Table Browser as a tool for accessing/exporting track data.
Guided walkthrough documents assembly, track, table, region, output choices, filters and intersection behavior.
The tutorial notes genome-wide export may be unavailable for large tracks and filter settings persist until cleared.
limitations: No exact assembly, track accession/version, query output, or biological cohort is fixed in the tutorial; no dataset record is warranted.
Interactive server behavior and output were not tested; track contents can change over time.
A task would need pinned track data or a reproducible retrieval snapshot and explicit coordinate/build semantics.
